nodes.name: Lattice Hydrogenation of TiO2
nodes.procedure: H-TiO2 catalysts were synthesized by acid-metal treatment method, as illustrated in Figure 2a. Upon lattice hydrogenation, TiO2 underwent a notable color transition from white to grayish blue.
nodes.source_text: Guided by the theoretical predictions, H-TiO2 catalysts were synthesized by acid-metal treatment method, as illustrated in Figure 2a. Upon lattice hydrogenation, TiO2 underwent a notable color transition from white to grayish blue (inset of Figure 2b).

nodes.name: Oxygen Vacancy Engineering of TiO2
nodes.procedure: OV-TiO2 was prepared by oxygen vacancy engineering method.
nodes.source_text: To confirm the successful lattice hydrogen implantation and resulting structural modifications, we conducted detailed crystallographic characterization of TiO2, OV-TiO2 and H-TiO2 samples

nodes.name: Lattice Hydrogenation of WO3
nodes.procedure: H-WO3 was prepared by applying the lattice hydrogen engineering strategy to WO3 using similar acid-metal treatment method as for H-TiO2.
nodes.source_text: Furthermore, we demonstrated the generality of the developed approach by applying it to other semiconducting oxides (WO3, MoO3, and Nb2O5).

nodes.description: 2e- ORR performance in neutral media using RRDE
nodes.source_text: The 2e− ORR performance of H-TiO2, TiO2, and OV-TiO2 was evaluated in an O2-saturated 0.5 M Na2SO4 electrolyte using rotating ring-disk electrode (RRDE) measurements at 1600 rpm... The onset potential of H-TiO2 shifted to a more positive value of 0.575 V versus RHE, corresponding to an overpotential (η) of only 125 mV... The H2O2 selectivity of H-TiO2 exceeded 95% within the potential window of -0.2 - 0.5 V versus RHE... electron transfer number (n) of 2.02... Tafel slope of 62.3 mV dec−1.

nodes.description: Long-term H2O2 electrosynthesis stability at industrial current density
nodes.source_text: we subjected the H-TiO2 catalyst to a demanding long-term test at 200 mA cm−2. The system demonstrated exceptional durability, operating stably for over 100 h at a full-cell voltage of 1.2 V (with the cathode potential at -0.25 V versus RHE) while maintaining a Faradaic efficiency of ~95%... high H2O2 production rate of 13,968 mmol h−1 g−1... energy efficiency of 41.3%.
Following 8 h of continuous electrolysis, the accumulated H2O2 concentration of H-TiO2 reached 2843 ppm.

nodes.characterization_summary: H-TiO2 shows enhanced optical absorption 400-1000 nm with NIR tail indicating new impurity states; TiO2 shows color transition from white to grayish blue.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Upon lattice hydrogenation, TiO2 underwent a notable color transition from white to grayish blue (inset of Figure 2b). To quantitatively characterize these changes, we performed Ultraviolet-Visible-Near Infrared Diffuse Reflectance Spectroscopy (UV-vis-NIR DRS) measurements (Figure 2b).

nodes.characterization_summary: H-TiO2 preserves pristine anatase-phase structure of TiO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) analysis (Figure 2c) revealed that H-TiO2 preserved the pristine anatase-phase structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows (101) lattice spacing of 0.37 nm for H-TiO2 with uniform titanium atom peak intensities, confirming intact periodic atomic arrangements without vacancy defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-Resolution Transmission Electron Microscopy (HRTEM) coupled with line-scan intensity analyses (Figure 2d,e and Figure S13) precisely measured the (101) lattice spacing of H-TiO2 and TiO2, which correspond to an interlayer spacing of 0.37 nm...

nodes.characterization_summary: IDPC-STEM confirms perfect alignment of H-TiO2 crystal structure with theoretical model; oxygen line-scan shows peak splitting from O-H bond formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: IDPC-STEM. The comparative results in Figure 2f,g and Figure S14 demonstrate perfect alignment between the experimentally observed H-TiO2 crystal structure and the theoretical atomic projection model...

nodes.characterization_summary: H-TiO2 displays new signal at 6.3 ppm for Ti-O_{2C}-H protons confirming lattice hydrogen at low-coordination oxygen sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: after lattice hydrogen incorporation, the 1H NMR spectrum of H-TiO2 displays a pronounced change, with the appearance of a new, distinct signal at 6.3 ppm. This resonance can be unambiguously assigned to protons coordinated to two-coordinated oxygen atoms (Ti-O_{2C}-H).

nodes.characterization_summary: H-TiO2 Ti 2p peaks shift to lower binding energies with Ti^{3+} at 463.4 eV; O 1s shows peaks at 531.7 eV (O-H) and 529.9 eV (Ti-O) with enhanced O-H.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) demonstrated significant shifts of Ti2p_{3/2} and 2p_{1/2} peaks toward lower binding energies after lattice hydrogen implantation, accompanied by the emergence of a characteristic peak at 463.4 eV attributed to Ti^{3+} species (Figure S15a,b). The O1s spectrum revealed two deconvoluted peaks at 531.7 eV and 529.9 eV, corresponding to O-H and metal-O bonds, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: H-TiO2 shows decreased t2g(L3)/eg(L3) ratio and peak shift to lower energies, indicating Ti3+ formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Ti L-edge XAS spectra... H-TiO2 exhibits a significantly decreased t2g(L3)/eg(L3) value, along with the shifting of systematic peak toward lower energies unambiguously indicating the formation of Ti3+ species.

nodes.characterization_summary: H-TiO2 shows decreased t2g/eg value due to altered O 1s-2p hybridization, corroborating Ti3+ presence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The O K-edge XAS spectra (Figure S17b) further reveal a decreased t2g/eg value in H-TiO2, attributable to the altered hybridization between oxygen 1s and 2p orbitals...

nodes.characterization_summary: H-TiO2 displays single-electron spin signal at g=1.993 indicating unpaired electrons in Ti d-orbitals; absent in TiO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) measurements provided direct evidence... H-TiO2 displayed a pronounced single-electron spin signal at g = 1.993, which is however absent in TiO2.

nodes.characterization_summary: H-TiO2 shows potential-dependent *OOH peak at 780 cm⁻¹ in O2-saturated electrolyte; weak on TiO2 and absent in N2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: in situ Raman spectra of H-TiO2 in an O2 saturated electrolyte revealed a potential-dependent peak at 780 cm⁻¹, which is characteristic of the O-O stretching vibration of surface-adsorbed *OOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: H-TiO2 detects *OOH at ~1224 cm⁻¹ and adsorbed H2O2 at ~1390 cm⁻¹ with increasing intensity under cathodic polarization.
nodes.evidence_snippet: in situ ATR-FTIR analysis further detected characteristic bands for both *OOH (~1224 cm⁻¹) and adsorbed H2O2 (~1390 cm⁻¹) on the H-TiO2 surface...

nodes.characterization_summary: H-TiO2 shows onset potential 0.575 V vs RHE (η=125 mV), >95% H2O2 selectivity (-0.2 to 0.5 V vs RHE), n=2.02; superior to TiO2 and OV-TiO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the onset potential of H-TiO2 shifted to a more positive value of 0.575 V versus RHE... The H2O2 selectivity of H-TiO2 exceeded 95% within the potential window of -0.2 - 0.5 V versus RHE... The corresponding electron transfer number (n) of 2.02 is close to the theoretical value for the 2e- pathway (n = 2.00).

nodes.characterization_summary: H-TiO2 shows cathodic ORR peak at 0.45 V vs RHE with j_peak=-0.75 mA cm^{-2}, superior to TiO2 (-0.50 mA cm^{-2}) and OV-TiO2 (-0.40 mA cm^{-2}).
nodes.evidence_snippet: the H-TiO2 exhibited a distinct cathodic reduction peak at 0.45 V (versus RHE) with a peak current density of -0.75 mA cm^{-2}, surpassing those of TiO2 (-0.50 mA cm^{-2}) and OV-TiO2 (-0.40 mA cm^{-2}).
